name: An oligo
description: one synthetic DNA oligonucleotide as ordered and as stored — its name, sequence, synthesis scale and purification, what it is for, and where its tube is
phrases: the shape of an oligo record

name.description: the lab's name for it, unique within the project. Project-specific nomenclature: SynThera's are oGho<n>, numbered without gaps, and the next available is one past the highest in that repository alone. NOT unique across projects: 36 names in the indexed corpus carry more than one DIFFERENT sequence, which is a collision to be resolved by the principal, never merged and never decided by mtime or repo precedence

sequence.description: 5'->3'. IUPAC ambiguity codes are meaningful: they are what makes a library a library, and 154 rows in the indexed corpus use them — do not tighten this to [ACGT]+. Case often marks intent — a designed mismatch, or the annealing region — and is not significant to any tool

scale.description: synthesis scale as the vendor names it. Across 809 rows that state it, the only values are 25nm (726) and 100nm (83). LENGTH DETERMINES IT RATHER THAN MERELY PREDICTING IT: JCA 2026-09-14, "They don't sell >59 at 25nm scale" — so 60bp and above is at least 100nm, as a vendor constraint. A reader may therefore resolve an absent scale at any length, and a RECORDED 25nm at 60bp or more is an error rather than a fact: sixteen such rows exist across six repositories and describe orders IDT does not sell.

purification.description: PRESENT means ordered this way; ABSENT means not recorded. Across 809 rows that state it, STD — standard desalting, i.e. no purification — is the only value that occurs

description.description: what it is for, in the words that will make sense a year later — 'Reverse p15A par A site library with 4 sites mutated', not 'reverse primer'

experiment.description: the experiment it was designed for

location.description: where the tube is, once it exists. Absent means not yet ordered or not yet filed

concentration.description: as labelled on the tube. 100 uM is the resuspended IDT stock; 10 uM is the PCR working stock; 2.66 uM is the sequencing working stock

source.description: WHERE THIS RECORD WAS READ FROM, and the only part of this object Cortex persists. A record is a pointer at a line in a file, never a copy of it: the file stays the truth, the object is parsed on demand, and nothing stored can drift from it

path.description: repo-relative path to the oligo file

line.description: 1-based line within that file. Must be >= 1; not expressible as a checked constraint here, because this store's validator refuses any keyword it cannot enforce rather than silently ignoring it

assumed.description: which of these values were INFERRED by the indexer rather than read from the file. An assumed value must never be indistinguishable from a recorded one — a re-order, an audit, or a person a year later has to be able to tell which is which. Sharpest inside the three files that carry both dialects, where the same column is fact on one row and a guess on the next. Absent or empty means every value here was read. Entries should not repeat; uniqueness is not expressible as a checked constraint here for the same reason as source.line

notes:
THE SERIALISATION IS THE IDT BULK ORDER FORM: tab-separated `name, sequence, scale, purification`, one per line, no header. The column order is not negotiable — it gets pasted into IDT's bulk input. SynThera's SLIP series and Cheese's Lactis/pBET series are written this way today. The description and the location live elsewhere precisely because IDT will not accept them. A record with a `location` is a tube; a record with `scale` and `purification` is an order; a record with neither is a known oligo.

REQUIRED IS [name, sequence], NOT ALL FOUR — revised 2026-09-14 after validating against 3,088 real oligo rows in 110 files across six repos. Requiring scale and purification rejected 74% of them, and those rows are not malformed: 1,933 are `name, sequence, description` (the lab's standing catalogue, jca-all_oligos.txt) and 348 are bare. The IDT form is a VIEW of this schema, not its floor. That this went unnoticed is its own finding: this schema had zero conforming instances and had never been run against anything.

DIALECT IS DECIDED PER ROW, NEVER PER FILE. Three files carry both forms — Oligos-pBET2.txt has bet007/bet008 with scale and purification and ce007/ce008 without, four lines apart; Lysis3 oligos.txt and pDel1 Oligos.txt do the same. A per-file sniff is the obvious reader design and is silently wrong on those, writing a scale onto rows that sit beside rows stating it — the worst case, because the file itself proves the value was not recorded for them.

ASSUMED VALUES FOR VESTIGIAL FILES. JCA 2026-09-14, on old files like jca-all_oligos.txt: assume no purification and 25 nmol. That is not a vendor guess — it is the observed house standard (see `scale` and `purification` above). The indexer may fill them in and MUST list what it filled in under `assumed`.

OLIGO POOLS ARE NOT OLIGOS. JCA 2026-09-14: *"oligopools are not oligos. They are different type because they are all mixed together. We shouldn't index individual oligos as though they are oligos."* An oPool order form (TPcon6/Tlib2, Tlib3 — columns `Pool name`, `Sequence`, 243 rows) lists the members of ONE tube in which everything is mixed: a member cannot be pipetted, has no name, and has no separate physical existence. Read as oligos they would produce 181 records all called Tlib3, each claiming to be a thing you could fetch. A reader MUST skip these files; they want a record type of their own, closer to a library than to an oligo.

INSTANCES ARE WRAPPERS, NOT COPIES — revised 2026-09-14. This note previously read "there are no oligo datums here and there should not be", reasoning that copying lines into the store would make a second copy of the freezer that drifts from the first. THAT REASONING STANDS and the conclusion was too broad: what it forbids is a COPY that drifts. A record carrying `source: {path, line}` is a pointer, re-parsed from the file on every query rather than maintained, so it has nothing to drift from. No oligo copies; wrappers are how they are reached.

INDEXED THREE WAYS, each answering what the others cannot: `name`; the full `sequence` uppercased, for IDENTITY (do we already have this oligo); and THE LAST 6 BASES, for ANNEALING (which oligos could prime on this template). Six is the biological floor — a polymerase requires a perfect 3' match — so a 6bp sliding window over a template rules out every non-candidate in a single lookup, turning alignment from O(oligos x template) into O(template). Measured: 62% of positions eliminated outright, median 1 candidate on the rest, and scan time flat from 250 to 26,580 oligos. A LONGER k IS NOT A SPEED OPTION, IT IS A CORRECTNESS LOSS: it silently discards anneals with 6-11bp of 3' identity. Zero of 3,088 oligos carry an ambiguity code in their last 6 bases — biology, not luck, since a degenerate 3' end will not prime — so one key each suffices, but an indexer must CHECK rather than assume it and must never index a literal N that then silently never matches.
